facts.statement: Listracanthus shaoyangensis was described as a new species by Fang et al.
facts.quote:
Name: Listracanthus shaoyangensis
Novelty: Sp. nov
Authors: Fang et al.

facts.statement: The species dates to the Permian Wuchiapingian age.
Its type locality is the Longtan Formation in China.
facts.quote:
Type locality: Longtan Formation
Country: China

facts.statement: Listracanthus first appeared in late Carboniferous strata in North America and disappeared from the fossil record during the Early Triassic.
facts.quote: Listracanthus first appeared in late Carboniferous strata in North America, and eventually disappear from the fossil record some time during the Early Triassic.

facts.statement: Species of Listracanthus are known mainly from huge feather‑like denticles that can be up to four inches long.
facts.quote: Species of Listracanthus are known primarily from their tremendous, feather-like denticles, which range up to four inches in length.

facts.statement: Each denticle has a large central spine with secondary spines projecting from its sides like feather barbs.
facts.quote: The denticles had a large main spine, from which secondary spines emanate from the sides, like the barbs of a feather or a comb.

facts.statement: Listracanthus is an extinct chondrichthyan whose precise evolutionary relationships are uncertain.
facts.quote: Listracanthus is a genus of extinct chondrichthyan with uncertain affinities.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest that Listracanthus may belong to the Menaspiformes group because its denticles are found with menaspiform remains.
facts.quote: other authors have noted that Listracanthus-like denticles have been found associated with the remains of Menaspiformes like Deltoptychius (which do not have eel-like bodies), and have suggested that Listracanthus is a member of this group.

facts.statement: Martill and colleagues erected the family Listracanthidae to include the genera Listracanthus and Acanthorhachis.
facts.quote: They also erected the family Listracanthidae to encompass the two genera.

facts.statement: The genus Acanthorhachis was created for the species formerly known as "Listracanthus" spinatus.
facts.quote: Martill et al., (2014) created the genus Acanthorhachis for the species formerly known as "Listracanthus" spinatus (Bolton, 1896).

facts.statement: Listracanthus is placed in the order Eugeneodontiformes and the family Edestidae.
